status_summary: Executive Order 14153 (2025-01-20) directed Interior to evaluate rescinding Public Land Order 5150. Public Land Order 7966, published 2026-02-25, partially revoked Orders 5150 and 5180 on about 2.1 million acres of the Dalton Utility Corridor, which Interior said makes that land available for state selection. Environmental groups sued on 2026-03-10; on 2026-07-24 the court dismissed claims covering about 1.38 million acres tentatively approved for conveyance to the State, denied a preliminary injunction on the remaining roughly 700,000 acres and kept those claims pending. Revocation of the other old orders the Mandate names was not found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14153 signed, directing Interior to evaluate changes to, including possible rescission of, Public Land Order 5150 and to review orders withdrawing lands for Alaska Native corporation selection.
Interior announced it would issue Public Land Order 7966, revoking Orders 5150 and 5180 in the Dalton Utility Corridor and making about 2.1 million acres available for state selection.
Public Land Order 7966 published, partially revoking Orders 5150 and 5180 on about 2,127,845 acres and opening the lands to the public land and mining laws from 2026-03-27.
Ten environmental groups sued in the District of Alaska challenging Public Land Order 7966 (Northern Alaska Environmental Center v. Burgum).
A law firm summary reports Interior conveyed about 1.4 million acres to the State; the State moved to dismiss on 2026-05-07.

The court dismissed claims as to about 1.38 million acres already tentatively approved for conveyance, on state sovereign immunity grounds, denied a preliminary injunction on the remaining roughly 700,000 acres, and kept those remaining claims.
